about:
# VertiCrop – 9:16 vertical crop frame for YouTube Shorts, TikTok and Reels in World of Warcraft

[![Release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/KesaObscura/VertiCrop)](https://github.com/KesaObscura/VertiCrop/releases/latest)
[![CurseForge](https://img.shields.io/curseforge/dt/1746139?label=CurseForge)](https://www.curseforge.com/wow/addons/verticrop)
[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/github/license/KesaObscura/VertiCrop)](https://github.com/KesaObscura/VertiCrop/blob/main/LICENSE)

A World of Warcraft addon for **content creators**. It draws the **9:16 crop frame** of a vertical
video over the game and marks the **safe zones** of **YouTube Shorts, TikTok and Instagram Reels**:
the parts the app covers with its top bar, captions and buttons. Place your character, cast bar,
unit frames and the rest of your UI for vertical video **before** you record, instead of finding
out in the editor that the important part ended up under the like button.

One download for **Retail (Midnight), Classic Era, TBC Anniversary, Wrath and Cataclysm
Classic, Mists of Pandaria Classic and WoW Forever**. 9 languages. Tested in game on WoW Forever,
Classic Era, TBC Anniversary and Mists of Pandaria Classic; on Retail, tell us how it works for
you.

![Lay out your UI for 9:16 in game and see what the phone will show](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/KesaObscura/VertiCrop/main/docs/gallery/01_hero.png)

| Before and after | Layout and recording mode | Works with Edit Mode |
|---|---|---|
| ![UI frames outside the crop, then everything inside the safe box](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/KesaObscura/VertiCrop/main/docs/gallery/02_before_after.png) | ![Safe zones while you set up, a clean frame while you record](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/KesaObscura/VertiCrop/main/docs/gallery/03_layout_and_recording.png) | ![A saved Edit Mode layout just for recording](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/KesaObscura/VertiCrop/main/docs/gallery/05_edit_mode.png) |

## Features

- **9:16 crop frame** in the middle of the screen, full screen height. Also **4:5** (Instagram feed),
  **1:1** and **16:9** for ultrawide screens (21:9, 32:9).
- **Darkened outside** (0–100 %), so you see at once what stays in the video.
- **Dead zones** (red): the safe-zone margins of YouTube Shorts, TikTok, Instagram Reels, or **All** (the largest margin
  of every side), with names on them.
- **Safe box** (yellow): keep what matters inside it and it stays visible even with long
  captions, automatic subtitles and on tall phones (19.5:9, 20:9) that cut the sides of a 9:16
  video. Above the side buttons it steps out to the right, so the top right corner is usable.
- **Grid**: rule-of-thirds lines and the center cross.
- **Move combat text**: the game's own floating combat text about you (damage taken, heals
  received) starts where you drag it: off your character, next to your unit frames, wherever it
  reads best in the clip, and drawn above other frames. Font, colours and float mode stay the
  game's; the game's self combat text must be on in its options.
- **Recording mode**: hides everything inside the frame. Only the dark sides and a thin border
  stay, **outside** the frame, so cropping the recording cuts them away. Record your gameplay with
  the frame on. The recording key ends it with the overlay hidden, so no zones flash at the end
  of a clip or a saved replay.
- **Crop values for OBS** in pixels: width, height, left, right, and top and bottom when the
  screen is narrower than the format (`/vcrop px` or the settings window). Enter them in the
  crop of the game capture item in OBS (*Edit Transform*, Ctrl+E) or in your video editor.
- Lines stay 1–2 screen pixels thick at any UI scale; the frame follows resolution and UI scale
  changes.
- **Off at every login**: a tool for setting up and recording, not for playing. `/vcrop` or your
  key binding switches it on; all other settings are kept.
- **Settings window** (`/vcrop opt`), also in the game's *Options → AddOns* and in the addon menu
  at the minimap on Retail and WoW Forever (left click: settings, right click: overlay on/off). Every option explains
  itself on hover.
- **Key bindings** (*Options → Key Bindings*, entries starting with "VertiCrop:"): overlay on/off, recording mode on/off,
  settings.
- 9 languages: English, Deutsch, Español, Français, Русский, 한국어, Português, 简体中文, 繁體中文.
  The addon follows your game language.

The safe zones are **approximate**: they are rounded from measured 1080×1920 layouts of the apps,
and the apps change their layout from time to time. Check your video in the app before you post.

## How to use it

1. `/vcrop opt`, choose the format and the platform.
2. Move your UI so that what matters is inside the yellow safe box and out of the red. On Retail
   and WoW Forever save a separate Edit Mode layout just for recording; on Classic use your UI
   addon (for example MoveAny or Bartender).
3. Optional: tick *Move combat text*, click *Move...* and drag the box to where your own damage
   and heal numbers should start. Numbers over enemies are drawn by the game and cannot be moved.
4. `/vcrop rec` (or the key binding) and record the full screen: in OBS a *Game Capture* source
   (or a *Window Capture* of the game, client area only).
5. Crop the recording with the values from `/vcrop px` (in your editor, or in OBS, see below)
   and scale it to 1080×1920. On a 1080p screen the 9:16 crop is only 608×1080 (on a 1366×768
   laptop 432×768); a 1440p screen gives a sharper clip.

## Tips for a UI that reads on a phone

- Out of the frame: chat, minimap, quest tracker, bags and the micro menu, and every action bar
  you do not press in the clip. They only cost space on a phone screen.
- In the safe box: player and target frame (the target frame left of the button zone), your cast
  bar, made bigger, and one small bar with the 4–6 spells the clip is about.
- Raise the UI scale or the scale of the frames you keep: a phone shows the frame at about a
  third of your monitor's width.
- Camera a bit closer than usual, the character slightly below the middle of the frame.

## Recording straight to 9:16 in OBS

- **Crop afterwards:** record the full screen with recording mode on, then crop in your editor
  with the values from `/vcrop px`. The crop is centred, so a 9:16 project with "fill" gives the
  same picture.
- **Vertical canvas:** set the OBS canvas (or a second vertical canvas, for example with the
  Aitum Vertical plugin or the vertical output of newer OBS) to 1080×1920, add your game capture,
  right-click it → *Transform → Edit Transform* (Ctrl+E) and enter the values from `/vcrop px` in
  *Crop*, then *Transform → Stretch to screen*. OBS then records a ready vertical file. Do not
  use a *Crop/Pad* filter for this: a filter belongs to the source and crops it on every canvas,
  your 16:9 stream too.
- **Templates for your editor:** transparent 1080×1920 PNGs with the same dead zones and safe
  box, one per platform, in [`docs/templates`](https://github.com/KesaObscura/VertiCrop/blob/main/docs/templates) (also attached to the releases).
  Put one on top of your clip in CapCut, DaVinci Resolve or Premiere to check the edit.
- **Streaming in 16:9 at the same time:** your viewers see the overlay too. Use it to lay out
  your UI, then switch it off with `/vcrop`: the crop values stay the same.
- The values count in pixels of the game window. If OBS records in another resolution than the
  game runs, scale them by the same factor.

## Commands

| Command | Does |
|---|---|
| `/vcrop` | overlay on/off (it starts off at every login) |
| `/vcrop rec` | recording mode on/off |
| `/vcrop opt` | settings window |
| `/vcrop px` | crop values for OBS in pixels |
| `/vcrop 9:16` / `4:5` / `1:1` / `16:9` | switch the format |
| `/vcrop reset` | all settings back to the defaults |

`/verticrop` works as well.

## FAQ

- **Does the frame end up in my video?** Not inside the crop. In recording mode everything the
  addon draws sits outside the frame, and the crop cuts it away. If you also keep the full 16:9
  recording or stream it, switch the overlay off with `/vcrop` (at 0 % darkening the thin border
  still shows).
- **Does it change my UI?** No. It only draws on top of the screen; it never moves, hides or
  resizes other frames (only the game's combat text, if you tick *Move combat text*), and it does
  not take mouse clicks.
- **Which game versions?** Retail, Classic Era, TBC Anniversary, Wrath and Cataclysm Classic, Mists of Pandaria Classic and WoW Forever, from
  one download.
- **Missing a platform or a format?** Open an issue: requests are read.

## Install

Install it from [CurseForge](https://www.curseforge.com/wow/addons/verticrop) (the CurseForge app keeps it up to date), or download a release zip and
unpack it into `<game folder>/_retail_/Interface/AddOns/` (or `_classic_era_`, `_classic_`, or your
WoW Forever client folder). The result must be `Interface/AddOns/VertiCrop/VertiCrop.toc`. With
GitHub's "Download ZIP", rename the folder from `VertiCrop-main` to `VertiCrop`, otherwise the game
does not load it.

## Bug reports

Please open an [issue](https://github.com/KesaObscura/VertiCrop/issues) with your game version
(Retail, Classic Era, ...), your screen resolution, what you did and what you expected. Lua errors
are easiest to read with BugGrabber + BugSack.

## Development

Plain Lua 5.1, no libraries. Files load in TOC order: `Locale.lua` → `Core.lua` → `TextMover.lua` →
`Options.lua`;
`Bindings.xml` is loaded by the game. Checkboxes, radio buttons and the slider are built from
textures every client ships, not from Blizzard templates, because those differ between game
versions.

Tests run outside the game against a small mock of the WoW API:

```
lua5.1 tests/run.lua
```

They cover the frame and safe-zone geometry, the OBS pixel values, the overlay in every mode, the
settings window (every control has a tooltip), slash commands, key bindings, the TOC and the locale
tables (every language has every key with the same placeholders). The `tests` folder is not part of
the release zip (see `.pkgmeta`).

**Translations**: all texts are in `Locale.lua`. Every language must have exactly the keys of `enUS`
with the same `%d` placeholders; `tests/run.lua` checks that.

## License

[MIT](https://github.com/KesaObscura/VertiCrop/blob/main/LICENSE)

releases.name: VertiCrop 1.5.0 — move combat text
releases.notes:
See the 9:16 crop of your vertical video in World of Warcraft: crop frame, YouTube Shorts / TikTok / Instagram Reels dead zones, safe box, recording mode and exact crop values for OBS.

**Install:** CurseForge app, or unpack the zip into `Interface/AddOns/` (the result must be `Interface/AddOns/VertiCrop/VertiCrop.toc`).

### What's new
- **Move combat text**: your own damage and heal numbers start where you drag a small box, for example inside the 9:16 frame, drawn above other frames. Font, colours and float mode stay the game's. Safe with WoW Forever's secret combat values.
- The frame is the OBS crop to the pixel: no border or darkening in your video.
- Easier to read on any ground: solid red edges, light line shadows, larger labels.
- Crop values show top and bottom when needed (16:9 on 16:10 screens, odd window sizes).
- Recording mode is off after every login, /reload keeps it; the recording key always gives a clean frame.
- The settings key and `/vcrop opt` open and close the window; key bindings are named "VertiCrop: …".
- Options → AddOns lists the commands and keeps the VertiCrop window open.

Full list: CHANGELOG.md. Bugs and wishes: https://github.com/KesaObscura/VertiCrop/issues

releases.name: VertiCrop 1.4.1 – tooltip and right click in the addon menu
releases.notes:
Addon menu at the minimap: a tooltip shows whether the overlay and recording mode are on, and what a click does. Left click opens the settings, right click switches the overlay on or off.

**Install:** the CurseForge app, or unzip `VertiCrop-1.4.1.zip` into `Interface/AddOns/`.

**Bugs and ideas:** [open an issue](https://github.com/KesaObscura/VertiCrop/issues) with your game version and screen resolution.

releases.name: VertiCrop 1.4.0 – 16:9 format for ultrawide screens
releases.notes:
New format 16:9 for ultrawide screens (21:9, 32:9): see which part of the screen a normal YouTube video keeps, with the crop values for OBS (on 3440 × 1440: 2560 × 1440, left 440, right 440). `/vcrop 16:9` switches to it.

**Install:** the CurseForge app, or unzip `VertiCrop-1.4.0.zip` into `Interface/AddOns/`.

**Bugs and ideas:** [open an issue](https://github.com/KesaObscura/VertiCrop/issues) with your game version and screen resolution.

releases.name: VertiCrop 1.3.2 – settings window remembers its place
releases.notes:
The settings window remembers where you dragged it, also after /reload and the next login. Reset keeps the place.

**Install:** the CurseForge app, or unzip `VertiCrop-1.3.2.zip` into `Interface/AddOns/`.

**Bugs and ideas:** [open an issue](https://github.com/KesaObscura/VertiCrop/issues) with your game version and screen resolution.

releases.name: VertiCrop 1.3.1 – dead zones, every setting on one line
releases.notes:
The red zones are called "Dead zones" now — the old name "Safe zones (red)" read as if red were safe, next to the yellow safe box. The settings window is a little wider, and every text in it fits on one line in every language; the crop values for OBS are shown on two lines.

**Install:** the CurseForge app, or unzip `VertiCrop-1.3.1.zip` into `Interface/AddOns/`.

**Bugs and ideas:** [open an issue](https://github.com/KesaObscura/VertiCrop/issues) with your game version and screen resolution.
